title: Jacobs to support next phase of growth at Dallas Fort Worth International Airport
summary: Jacobs has been selected by Dallas Fort Worth International Airport to lead design of Skylink modifications as part of the Terminal F Expansion Project.
body_markdown:
DALLAS –


[Jacobs](http://www.jacobs.com/) (NYSE: J) h


as been selected by Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) to lead design of Skylink modifications as part of the


[Terminal F Expansion Project](https://www.dfwairport.com/construction/terminal-f/) . The work will enable the addition of up to 16 new gates at the airport’s future Terminal F, supporting continued regional air travel growth.


With more than 87 million annual passengers, DFW is one of the


[world’s busiest airports.](https://www.dfwairport.com/dfwnewsroom/dfw-remains-worlds-third-busiest-airport-for-passenger-traffic/)


Relying on Skylink, its automated light rail train, DFW maintains fast, secure airside connections across its expansive, multi


‑


terminal footprint. The Terminal F modifications project involves alterations to existing Skylink guideway bridge spans, integrating complex bridge and structural design with the challenge of maintaining full system operability throughout all phases of construction.


Leveraging its proven design delivery expertise, Jacobs will collaborate with the Innovation Next+ construction joint venture, to provide intelligent design solutions to specifically optimize construction sequencing, operational requirements and safety considerations. This collaborative approach enables better decision‑making and reduced risk, supporting efficient phasing in a highly constrained, active airport environment that maintains passenger mobility while unlocking future capacity.


**Jacobs Executive Vice President Tom Meinhart said:** “DFW continues to raise the bar for innovation, scale and the passenger experience. This project is about taking infrastructure that already works and finding smarter ways to adapt and extend it to support the airport’s next phase of growth. Keeping Skylink running throughout construction is no small task, and it speaks to our focus on thoughtful phasing, practical design and creative engineering that keeps people and commerce moving.”


The modifications will allow construction of dual parallel taxi lanes beneath the light rail to integrate new Terminal F facilities with DFW’s established taxiway network, extending the useful life of existing infrastructure while minimizing disruption to airport operations and customer experience.


[Ranked No. 1 in Aviation](https://www.jacobs.com/about/industry-recognition) by


*Engineering News‑Record* , Jacobs brings industry‑leading experience delivering complex


[airport programs](https://www.jacobs.com/industries/aviation) through collaborative delivery models, including design‑build. From airside infrastructure and people mover systems to terminal expansions and structural retrofits, Jacobs helps airport owners manage risk, maintain operations and unlock capacity while enhancing safety, resilience and the passenger experience.
